ventral_fluke_pixel_intensity_distributi.global_contrast_ratio: Predominantly low-intensity (dark-gray/black) pixel mass across 98% of the visible surface area, with high-intensity (white/light-gray) pixels limited to discrete circular outlines and marginal calcifications.
ventral_fluke_pixel_intensity_distributi.spatial_color_mapping: The 2D area is defined by a monolithic dark-gray region. Distinctive light-gray circular rings (approx. 10-15 pixels in diameter) are mapped at central coordinates relative to the median notch and on the lower-lateral quadrants of both lobes.

trailing_edge_2d_geometric_contour.median_notch_angle: Deep V-shaped central depression with a calculated internal pixel angle of approximately 42 degrees; symmetric depth relative to the fluke lobes.
trailing_edge_2d_geometric_contour.edge_topography_serration_map: High-frequency, irregular serration profile along the entire length of the trailing edge. Pixel amplitudes of peaks range from 6 to 18 pixels, with higher density and sharper gradients on the distal third of both lobes.
trailing_edge_2d_geometric_contour.lobe_sweep_trajectory: Sigmoidal curve characterized by a concave transition from the median notch followed by a pronounced convex curve extending to the upward-swept lateral tips.

localized_surface_anomalies.rosette_scar_constellations: Multiple circular, high-contrast light-gray outlines (rosettes) observed in the central and lower-left regions of the dark fluke surface.

acquired_anomalies_or_scars: High-intensity white pixel clusters exhibiting irregular topography consistent with calcified external growth (barnacles), localized exclusively on the extreme lateral tips and sporadic points along the trailing edge serrations.
